description: The spec dictionary: how S2A names, structures, tokenizes and makes accessible each role a design can play. specs:scaffold reads extracted Figma evidence (roles, axes, layers) through this file to draft a <slug>.defs.json in the library's conventions, so every component enters the contract system the same way. Tokens here must be shipped semantic tokens (npm run defs:validate checks).

naming.set: PascalCase component name; the Figma set and the code export share it
naming.slug: lowercase-kebab of the name; folder, file and story ids
naming.partClass: {abbr}-{part} where abbr is the slug's initials (quote-card → qc)
naming.figmaPart: .{part} (dot-prefixed, kebab-case; text layers match the text property name)

lever.name: mediaSrc
lever.notes: Decorative art; aria-hidden. Use a real Media instance in Figma so the swap is a property, not raw layers.

lever.name: icon
lever.notes: Icon name resolved by the AppIcon / icon set; decorative unless it is the only content.

lever.name: headline
lever.notes: The card's accessible name when the whole card is a link.

divider.notes: 1px is a Primitive exception recorded in decisions; Divider is also an S2A component if the rule needs its own props.

lever.name: ctaLabel
lever.notes: Visible label of the action; empty when the affordance is a chevron alone (then the headline carries the accessible name).

chevron.notes: Decorative arrow; never the only indication of the link (WCAG 1.4.1).

text.question: A text layer carries no recognisable role (not heading, body, eyebrow or label). Is it content (add a lever) or part of the illustration (fold into media)?

link-card.description: A card that is one link: illustration or icon, a headline, optional description, an arrow affordance. The whole surface is the target and the headline is the accessible name.
link-card.when: roles include heading and cta and the frame does not repeat a unit

root.notes: Block-level link; content stacks vertically and the CTA row pins to the bottom. Hover and focus change the surface, never only the colour of the arrow.

props.name: target
props.notes: Integration detail; new-window links append an accessible hint.

keyboard.action: moves focus to the card as one stop

notes: One link, one accessible name: the headline text. Media, icon and chevron are aria-hidden so the name is not padded with noise.
No interactive element may be nested inside the card (a link inside a link is invalid HTML and unreachable by keyboard).
Focus ring is drawn on the whole card surface (2.4.7) and the target is at least 24×24 (2.5.8).
Headline and description meet 4.5:1 on the card surface; the chevron and any border meet 3:1 (1.4.3, 1.4.11).
The arrow is decorative: link purpose comes from the headline text (2.4.4), not from the glyph alone (1.4.1).

card.description: A non-interactive content card; actions live in a slot.
card.when: roles include heading and the frame does not repeat a unit; no cta role

notes: Actions inside the card are native links or buttons; the card itself has no role.

collection.description: A row, grid or scroller of one repeated unit.

props.name: layout
props.notes: row at wide viewports, scroll on phones; grid when the count exceeds one row.

states.name: Breakpoint
states.notes: A layout response, not an authored prop.

notes: List semantics: ul/li so the count is announced.
Horizontal scroll must be reachable by keyboard and must not trap focus; content reflows at 320px without two-dimensional scrolling.

button.description: Triggers an action. A label, optional leading and trailing icons, and the full interactive state set.
button.when: binds the button token namespace, or a State axis with hover/active/focus/disabled

notes: Renders a native <button>, or an <a> when it navigates — never a div with a click handler.
The label is the accessible name; an icon-only button needs an aria-label.
Focus is visible on the control itself (2.4.7) and the target is at least 24x24 (2.5.8).
Disabled is conveyed to assistive tech, not by colour alone (1.4.1).

checkbox / radio.description: A selection control with a checked state, usually paired with a label.
checkbox / radio.when: a two-value Selected or Checked axis, usually beside a label

notes: Native input with a real <label>, so the hit area includes the text.
Indeterminate is a property, not a third value.
Group related controls in a fieldset with a legend (1.3.1).

behaviour.input: a native <input type=checkbox|radio> inside the <label>, visually hidden but focusable; checked reflects the selected prop, disabled/name/value pass through
behaviour.control: the drawn control (ring, box, dot, check) is decoration: aria-hidden, keyed off the root's data attribute so it follows the native input
behaviour.keyboard: Space toggles a checkbox; arrow keys move within a radio group; nothing else is interactive
behaviour.motion: none required; a short transition on the indicator is acceptable, respect prefers-reduced-motion

toggle / switch.description: A binary on/off control that applies immediately.
toggle / switch.when: a State axis of on/off, or a Checked boolean with switch semantics

notes: role=switch with aria-checked; it is not a checkbox and does not wait for submit.
State must not be carried by colour alone (1.4.1).

input / field.description: Accepts typed input. Label, value, placeholder, and an error state.
input / field.when: a TEXT axis for value or placeholder plus an error or focus state

notes: A visible label, programmatically associated — placeholder is not a label (3.3.2).
Errors say what is wrong and how to fix it, in text (3.3.1).
aria-describedby ties helper and error text to the field.

badge / tag / chip.description: A small label. Non-interactive unless it is dismissible.
badge / tag / chip.when: no state axis and no interactive states; a short text axis

notes: Not a button. If it dismisses, the dismiss affordance is the control, not the tag.
Meaning never rests on colour alone (1.4.1).

pagination.when: a repeated indicator unit with a current/selected state

notes: A nav landmark with an accessible name.
The current page is aria-current, not just a colour change.
Every indicator is reachable and activatable by keyboard (2.1.1).

accordion.description: A disclosure: a trigger that shows and hides a region of content. Open or closed is a prop a consumer sets, not an interaction state.
accordion.when: a State axis of open|closed (or expanded|collapsed), a trigger layer and a content layer

behaviour.trigger: a native <button> with aria-expanded reflecting `open` and aria-controls pointing at the content region
behaviour.content: a region (role=region, aria-labelledby the trigger) that is hidden when closed — hidden attribute, not display:none alone, so it is out of the accessibility tree too
behaviour.keyboard: Enter and Space on the trigger toggle it; nothing else is interactive
behaviour.motion: expand and collapse are transitions on the content's height or grid-template-rows; respect prefers-reduced-motion

notes: The trigger is a real <button>; aria-expanded is the state, aria-controls the relationship (4.1.2).
Closed content is hidden from everyone, not only visually (1.3.1).
Keyboard: Enter/Space toggles; focus stays on the trigger (2.1.1).

select / dropdown.description: A choice among options. The native <select> does the choosing; the design styles the trigger around it.
select / dropdown.when: a trigger layer with a chevron and a menu of options, or a .select/.trigger hidden set

behaviour.control: a native <select> is the control — keyboard, screen reader and mobile pickers come for free; the styled trigger is its visual, never a div that pretends
behaviour.label: a visible <label for> or aria-labelledby; a placeholder is not a label
behaviour.menu: the options list is the browser's unless the design needs rich option content, in which case it becomes a listbox (role=listbox/option) with full keyboard support — a separate, larger contract

notes: Native <select> keeps name, role and value correct without ARIA (4.1.2).
Every select has a programmatic label (3.3.2).
Arrow keys change the value; Space/Enter opens (2.1.1).

helper text.description: Guidance or a message under a field: hint, error, success. Associated with its field, never floating.
helper text.when: a short text layer with an optional leading icon, named helper, hint, message or error

behaviour.association: the field's aria-describedby names this element's id; an error also sets aria-invalid on the field
behaviour.live: an error that appears on submit is announced: role=alert or aria-live=polite on the message container

notes: Described-by is the relationship; colour alone is not the error signal (1.4.1, 3.3.1).
The message says what is wrong and, where possible, how to fix it (3.3.3).

list.description: A sequence of like items — features, links, steps. The items are the content; the list is the rhythm.
list.when: a repeated child layer (ListItem, Item) under a vertical frame

behaviour.items: each item is an <li>; an item with a leading icon keeps the icon decorative (aria-hidden) unless it carries meaning

notes: A real <ul>/<li> so the count and position are announced (1.3.1).

unboundPaint.question: {count} painted layers carry no variable ({list}). Bind them to S2A tokens in Figma, or record a raw: exception with the reason.
unboundPaint.fix: Bind the paints in Figma and re-publish evidence, or note the exception on the part in anatomy.

genericLayers.question: {count} layers carry Figma-generated names ({list}). Build set from this contract produces the normalized set (.root, .part names); replace the frame with it once reviewed.
genericLayers.fix: Run Build set from this contract, then re-anchor anchors.figma.nodeId to the normalized set.

codePending.question: No code exists yet. Generate {importPath} from the spec (/spec-to-html), run npm run evidence:code -- --slug={slug}, then remove anchors.code.pending.
codePending.fix: Once {importPath} exists, run npm run evidence:code -- --slug={slug} and delete anchors.code.pending.

archetype.question: Scaffolded as {archetype} ({why}). Confirm, or re-run npm run specs:scaffold -- --slug={slug} --archetype=<link-card|card|collection>.

levers.question: Levers were derived from roles ({roles}), not from component properties. Confirm names and which are authored (lever true) versus integration (lever false).
levers.fix: Edit props[] in this file: rename a lever, or set lever:false where it is integration rather than authoring.

match.question: Structural match says {verdict}: closest existing contract is {name} (score {score}). Extend it instead of adding a component?
match.chose: a new component, over extending {name} (match {verdict}, score {score})
match.fix: If it is the same component, delete this draft and add a variant to {name} instead.

strayText.fix: Name the layer in Figma so it claims a role, or add it under anatomy.root.parts here.

extraArt.fix: Fold the layers into the Media instance in Figma, or name them as parts in anatomy.
